core_obligations: Choose a presentation of the finitely presented module and record the finitely many coefficients of the entries of its matrix (proof lines 4690-4700).

Decompose the situation over a finitely generated subalgebra R_lambda of R containing those coefficients and a finite R_lambda-subalgebra S_lambda of S, and note that S is the directed colimit of these (proof lines 4700-4707).

Use the limit statement to find lambda such that the base changed module over S_lambda is flat, apply the finite Noetherian descent statement to conclude flatness over R_lambda, and pull the conclusion back by base change (proof lines 4707-4715).
proof_roadmap: Present the module and collect the coefficients (proof lines 4690-4700).
Approximate the situation by finitely generated subalgebras (proof lines 4700-4707).
Apply the limit statement and the finite case, then pull back (proof lines 4707-4719).
difficulty_reason: The lemma descends flatness of a finitely presented module along an injective integral extension, and the proof is a 30-line reduction to the finite Noetherian case. It chooses a presentation of the module, writes the entries of the presentation matrix as polynomials whose coefficients are finitely many elements of the base, and then decomposes the whole situation over a finitely generated subalgebra of the base with a finite subalgebra of the extension; flatness after base change is then inherited by one of these finitely generated pieces by the limit statement for flatness of finitely presented modules, the finite Noetherian case of the descent statement applies there, and the conclusion is pulled back by base change. The two reductions are the substance and both are displayed.
